question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,F=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An elementary matrix is a matrix obtained from the identity matrix by applying exactly one elementary row operation. 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrix $D$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $E$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $F$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

Therefore, only $E$ is an elementary matrix.
